question: Why are 0 and 1 the only numbers that equal their own square in p-adics?
answer: In base 10, two non-zero numbers can multiply to 0: 6 × 5 = 30 ends in 0, because 10 = 2 × 5. A prime base never does this, so n × (n − 1) = 0 forces n = 0 or n = 1.
move: Prime base: no zero-divisors, so only 0 and 1 are their own square.
